title: Open problem: Does a change of the aggregation unit move spatial-transcriptomics conclusions, and is the
statement: Does a change of the aggregation unit move spatial-transcriptomics conclusions, and is there a support above which they stop moving? Posed in print by name, in this field, and explicitly left unmeasured: the posing paper says the influence of the aggregation unit "is completely unknown and ignored" while noting that "there are well established approaches for quantifying the impact of the MAUP". The routed limb is the measurable one: for a pre-declared set of Visium HD and Stereo-seq datasets re-binned to a ladder of square supports, and for outputs well defined on an arbitrary areal support (an SVG rank list; a spatial-domain partition at fixed k), decompose each output's variance into a tissue-identity component and an aggregation-support component against a within-support resampling noise floor, and test whether a support s* exists above which the support component falls below that floor by a criterion declared before any data are pulled. Declare the ladder, the datasets, the methods and the criterion first, because both branches are substantive and the criterion is what makes them distinguishable. Use the owning field's existing instrument rather than inventing one: S-maup (PLOS ONE 2018, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0207377) is a formal MAUP-sensitivity statistic, and the geography literature's change-of-support machinery already covers this. Do NOT re-run the qualitative demonstration that bin size matters, which is published several times over: arXiv 2602.02825 "On the consistent and scalable detection of spatial patterns" already plots per-gene spatial-variability Z-scores at 8 um against 16 um on Visium HD ("comprising 164,800 bins at 16 um resolution, and 656,788 bins at 8 um") with outliers picked out, including that "the 'Swiss roll' pattern introduced during sample preparation was preferentially detected at 8 um resolution", attributed to "signal dampening at the 16 um Nyquist limit"; and FICTURE (bioRxiv 2023.11.04.565621) reports grid-size dependence qualitatively ("Making the grid smaller slightly improved the resolution but led to extremely noisy cluster assignments") as its motivation for going segmentation-free. Neither is an answer, and this ledger's verification pass narrowed what arXiv 2602.02825 is: the 8-vs-16 um contrast appears only in the full HTML text, is one illustrative cross-resolution sanity check inside a paper about a scalable spatial-pattern test, and carries no stability metric, no noise floor, no variance decomposition and no mention of MAUP. What is missing is the metric, the floor and the criterion, not another pair of supports. Do NOT treat STExplorer (Zormpas et al., bioRxiv 2025.01.17.633539) as having answered it: it names MAUP and Visium HD binning ("may introduce artificial ecotones by binning") and then fixes the support, its unit is the bin at one support and its estimand is a local non-stationary association. Do NOT treat the SVG and domain-detection benchmark family (Genome Biology 2024 and 2025; Bioinformatics 2025; NAR 2025) as prior art: their unit is the method and their endpoint is performance, all at fixed support. Two presuppositions must be carried as stated limitations rather than assumed away: re-binning only stands in for capture at that support, since real coarse capture also changes sensitivity and diffusion, so any measurement is a LOWER BOUND on support-dependence; and segmentation-based pipelines and cell-level cell-cell communication must be quarantined as a separate limb, because they presuppose cells rather than an arbitrary areal support. One further limb is NOT established and should be measured rather than assumed: that a non-trivial body of published conclusions actually rests on a default support. Read first, unopened by this ledger: the body of the Cell 2023 review "Mapping the transcriptome" (cell.com fulltext and PDF both client-errored; the White Rose eprint 218767 landing page was read and its keyword list includes "modifiable areal unit problem", but the PDF was not opened within budget) — it is the most likely place the posing already reaches into the target field's flagship venue, and it can only harden the case that the question is asked. Provenance: this is UQ-20261017-13's own canonical question, rejected at Gate 2 as asked-but-open rather than as a disguised known, since the import is explicit and under its own name.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: Comber A, Zormpas G, Queen R, Cockell S, "Lessons from spatial transcriptomics and computational geography in mapping the transcriptome", *AGILE: GIScience Series* 5:21 (2024), doi 10.5194/agile-giss-5-21-2024 — read in full and verified verbatim in the PDF body by a fresh-context checker: "The choice of aggregation unit will influence process understanding through scale (MAUP) driven distortions but this is completely unknown and ignored", alongside "there are well established approaches for quantifying the impact of the MAUP". It is a position piece: no data unit, no endpoint, no estimand, and it measures nothing. Corroborated as still open two ways. STExplorer (bioRxiv 2025.01.17.633539), from overlapping authorship, carries the named problem into the field's own literature and then fixes the support without testing it. And the quantity itself is unpublished: a mandatory query aimed squarely at the fraction of spatially variable genes that changes with bin size found it has never been reported, and a search for re-binning concordance of spatial-domain clustering (Stereo-seq bin20/bin50/bin100, ARI) found no such study — the comparators in that literature are methods, platforms and organs, never supports. Twenty documented searches across the target field in its own words, geography and geostatistics (MAUP, change of support, ecological fallacy), landscape ecology (grain and extent), signal processing (Nyquist), image downsampling and Chinese-language terms found no formulation that measures it. Caveat: the verbatim matches come from a page summariser rather than raw page text, and the Cell 2023 review body is unread.
inputs.tier: A — public Visium HD and Stereo-seq data exist down to 2 um, re-binning is arithmetic, the methods are installed and S-maup supplies the criterion; the binding constraint is pre-declaration discipline, not compute or access. The segmentation limb is B, since it needs a segmentation ground truth the binned limb does not.
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
